Asynchronous TypeScript and ES Modules

← Back to Course Package

Key Concepts

  • Modularity: The practice of breaking code into separate files (modules) to improve organization, scalability, and maintainability.
  • ECMAScript Modules (ESM): The modern standard for packaging JavaScript code using import and export statements.
  • Asynchronous Programming: A method allowing the program to start a task and wait for it to finish (like user input) without freezing the entire application.
  • Promises: Objects representing the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value.
  • Top-Level Await: A feature allowing developers to use the await keyword at the root level of a module without wrapping it in an async function.

Syntax / API Reference

Exporting Logic (finance.ts):

export const calculateInterest = (principal: number) => principal * 0.05;

Importing Built-in Modules:

import * as readline from 'node:readline/promises';

Importing Local Modules:

import { calculateInterest } from './finance.js';

Handling User Input:

const rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
const answer = await rl.question('Enter amount: ');

Step-by-Step Workflow

  1. Initialize Project: Run npm init -y to create your package.json.
  2. Install Dependencies: Run npm install -D typescript @types/node to set up the environment.
  3. Configure ESM: Add "type": "module" to your package.json file.
  4. Configure TypeScript: Set "target": "ESNext" and "module": "ESNext" in your tsconfig.json.
  5. Create Logic Module: Write your functions in a file (e.g., logic.ts) and use the export keyword.
  6. Build Main App: Import your logic and Node's readline/promises into app.ts using await for inputs.
  7. Compile and Run: Run npx tsc to generate JS files, then execute with node app.js.

Gotcha Alerts

  • ⚠️ The Extension Rule: When importing local files, you must use the .js extension in the path, even though your source file is .ts.
  • ⚠️ Package Type: If you forget to add "type": "module" to package.json, Node will treat your files as CommonJS and import will fail.
  • ⚠️ String Inputs: The readline.question() method always returns a string; use parseFloat() or Number() before doing math.
  • ⚠️ TSConfig Version: Top-level await will throw errors unless your tsconfig.json target is set to ES2022 or ESNext.

Key Takeaways

  • Transition from static code to interactive Command Line Interface (CLI) applications.
  • Successfully implement modular architecture by separating business logic from execution code.
  • Utilize modern import/export syntax over the legacy require method.
  • Manage asynchronous user interactions cleanly using await and readline/promises.
